lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say. Then practise develops listening and speaking by modelling pronunciation and giving students the chance to practise saying the target words or phrases with the correct intonation and stress at phrase level.
Look for careful listening, speaking fluency, confident repetition, and taking turns.

“It’s not easy finding all the places I want to visit. Can you help me find my way? I often get  lost and I can’t remember the directions… or what to ask! Let’s practise asking and answering for directions - then I’ll know where to go!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - B. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer develops speaking fluency by allowing students to practise using a simple question and answer format.
Look for pairs using the correct question forms, giving clear answers and taking turns during their short conversations.
“Do you have a travel buddy? Pair up and make sure you don’t get lost. Look at the map and work out where you need to go together.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.71 - A Look and write.

details: Look and write develops writing accuracy and comprehension by helping students match pictures to words and fill in the missing words using the prompts from the word box.
Look for correct answers and matching of pictures and words and neat handwriting.
“Oh no! Some of my directions have gone missing. Can you be a travel detective and help me find them? Let’s write them down so we don’t lose them again.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.71 - B Look and write.

details: Look and Write strengthens written accuracy and basic comprehension by having students interpret visual cues, choose the correct directional vocabulary, and form simple sentences that show they can connect images to meaning.
Look for clear sentences that match the directions shown, correct use of words like left/right/next to, good punctuation and neat handwriting.

Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - Speaking Board Game

details: Board game develops speaking and reading fluency and question and answer skills in the format of a fun game. It helps to build confidence through spontaneous language use.
Look for understanding the rules of the game, clear pronunciation, good use of question and answers and taking turns.
“Let’s have a travel adventure. Play the travel board game with a friend and see who can get the most points whilst visiting lots of attractions. Be careful! You can lose points too!”

Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.

Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

The Song provides the opportunity to recognise the target structure and vocabulary in a song as well as practising reading and listening skills.
Look for accurate reading as well as good pronunciation as they follow the lyrics and finally sing the song as a group
“Amazing! Well done children. We can talk about travel and directions. Let’s sing a song together to celebrate. Sing the words with me!”
